transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Lee... I'm here because, for over a year now, I've just been trying to get someone to take me seriously. 

At my job—I do computer support—they implemented this new ticket rotation and these regular security audits. And it's... well, it's clear to me that they're being used to build a paper trail against me. I've tried talking to management about it, but they just keep showing me the system logs and saying it's just standard company policy. But I know what I'm looking at, and it's been incredibly frustrating trying to get anyone to see what's actually going on.

During this past year, have you noticed any stretches of time where your mood was either unusually low and depressed, or unusually high, energetic, or irritable, separate from how you feel about the situation at work?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed and frustrated about what's happening at the office, obviously. It takes a toll on you, dealing with that every day. But other than that? My mood's been fine. I haven't had any periods of being really depressed or bouncing off the walls with energy or anything like that. It's just the situation at work that's the problem.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly normal. Like I said, the only thing going on is what they're doing with the audits at work.
Do you currently use alcohol, recreational drugs, or any new medications or supplements that could be contributing to how you've been feeling?

No, I don't use any of that. I'm not a drinker, and I definitely don't use any recreational drugs. I haven't started any new medications or supplements either. I just take my usual daily vitamin, but that's it. There's nothing like that affecting me. It's just... well, it's just the stress of what's happening at the office.
Outside of work, do you also feel that people—like family, friends, or neighbors—might be watching you, talking about you, or working against you in some way?

No, no, nothing like that. My family and friends are fine. My neighbors keep to themselves, mostly. I don't feel like anyone outside of work is watching me or against me. It's really just confined to the office and those audits I mentioned. Everything else in my life is pretty normal, to be honest.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out mood disorder (no manic/depressive episodes), psychotic disorder with hallucinations (denies), substance-induced psychosis (no substance use), and paranoid symptoms extending beyond work (confined to office). Encapsulated, non-bizarre persecutory delusion lasting over a year with preserved functioning elsewhere strongly supports delusional disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that workplace security audits and ticket rotations are being orchestrated to build a case against him) lasting over one year. The delusion is circumscribed to the work context, with no evidence of hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms that would suggest schizophrenia. Mood symptoms (mania or depression) were explicitly denied, ruling out a mood disorder with psychotic features. Substance use and medical contributions were ruled out. Functioning outside of the delusional belief system (family, friends, neighbors) remains intact, which is characteristic of delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia, where broader functional decline and additional psychotic symptoms are expected. The encapsulated, non-bizarre nature of the delusion with preserved overall functioning supports a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22).
